title: Signing commands: register, add-key, retire-key, endorse, approve, revoke
description: Write records and sign via ssh-keygen -Y sign (agent or key file); never touch private keys, never push. register builds person file from a pubkey; add-key/retire-key edit and re-sign with all current keys; endorse/approve/revoke write the records with correct namespaces.
acceptance_criteria: Each command's output passes git vouch check in a fixture registry; a person-file version signed only by a newly added key gives the D1 WARNING (not a failure), a version signed by a key in neither version fails check; commands never prompt.
notes:
Per DESIGN.md 2026-10-22: endorse writes subjectEmails (D2); 'register [--from FILE]' completes a git-vouch-migrate draft keeping migratedFrom; register/add-key --attestation BLOBFILE --challenge FILE embed {blob, challenge}; person-file signing needs any one key current in the previous version (D11).
Decisions (decision / alternative / why):
1. Write commands write into the registry checkout in the current directory / write into the synced copy that is DIR's default after setup / DESIGN.md says they write files for a registry merge request, and that needs a working checkout the user commits from; the synced copy is read-only cache for verification.
2. endorse subjectKey = the subject's first current key / take a --key option, or one endorsement per key / DESIGN.md's record names one key; the first current key is deterministic and needs no extra option (YAGNI).
3. endorse and approve refuse self-endorsement and self-approval at the CLI / write the record and let check report it as void / check's rule (void, not an error) is for records already in the registry; writing a record that check would void only helps a user who made a mistake. check's behaviour is unchanged.
4. revoke --reason defaults to 'compromise' and takes free text / a fixed enum / DESIGN.md's example uses 'compromise' and names no closed set; check does not interpret the reason.
5. Acceptance criterion 'add-key without an existing key's signature fails check': DESIGN.md (the person file rules, accepted risk with a WARNING) overrides it. A file signed only by the newly added key passes with a WARNING. Only a signature by a key in neither version fails, and test_add_key_without_an_existing_keys_signature asserts both / change check to fail / DESIGN.md is authoritative and the bead may not edit it. The owner may want to reword the criterion.
6. Review fixes: user.signingKey also accepts git's bare 'ssh-...' form; _write_signed follows no symlink in the checkout (O_NOFOLLOW dir chain, temp file plus rename); the prompt tests use an askpass trap and a pty; the docstring states that the sk-dummy attestation fixture is degenerate (empty cert, sig and authdata) and not a verification vector.
